scenes.say: Ever wonder which JVM flags are must-haves for running Java in production?

scenes.label: Heap
scenes.sub: Set heap size with Xmx and Xms for stability.
scenes.say: First, control your heap memory. Use Xmx and Xms to set max and initial heap size. This keeps your app stable under load.

scenes.title: Key JVM flags
scenes.say: Next, enable the G1 garbage collector for balanced performance, and turn on heap dumps for OutOfMemory errors. These help you troubleshoot fast.

rows.b: Heap as percent of container RAM

scenes.say: If you're running in containers, set MaxRAMPercentage and ActiveProcessorCount. This ensures the JVM uses only its allowed resources.

scenes.question: Is heap dump on OutOfMemory optional?
scenes.right: No, it's essential for post-mortem analysis.
scenes.say: Don't skip heap dumps. In production, they're critical for analyzing memory leaks after crashes.
